facts.statement: Mancalla fossils date from the Late Miocene to the Early Pliocene.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Late Miocene to Early Pliocene

facts.statement: The genus Mancalla was described by Lucas in 1901.
Mancalla californiensis is the type species of the genus Mancalla.
Four species are known: M. californiensis, M. cedrosensis, M. lucasi, and M. vegrandis.
facts.quote: subdivision: Mancalla californiensis Lucas, 1901 Mancalla cedrosensis Howard, 1971 Mancalla lucasi Smith, 2011 Mancalla vegrandis Smith, 2011

facts.statement: Mancalla was an extinct genus of flightless alcids.
facts.quote: Mancalla is an extinct genus of prehistoric flightless alcids

facts.statement: Mancalla lived on the Pacific coast of modern-day California and Mexico.
facts.quote: lived on the Pacific coast of today's California and Mexico

facts.statement: The Paleobiology Database lists the time range of Mancalla as the Messinian to the Late Pleistocene (7.246 to 0.0117 million years ago).
facts.quote: Time range: Messinian to Late Pleistocene (7.246 to 0.0117 million years ago)

facts.statement: There are 32 recorded fossil occurrences of Mancalla.
